Latin word

narrātiō

narrātiō, narrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an account, a telling of what happened; an account, a narrative

In this lexicon

  • account

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.80: rem narrāre ita ut vērīsimilis narrātiō sit (Lewis & Short); Cic. Or. 124 (Lewis & Short)

  • version

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.80: ut vērī similis narrātiō sit (Lewis & Short)

  • fābulōsa narrātiō: fiction

    modern

Notes

  1. 1narrātiō: short first a (Bennett’s nārrō). From narrō, which de Vaan (s.v. gnārus) derives from *nārāre, shortened by the littera-rule. Ruling: narrō with a short a.

Examples

  • dīcere quae audierint ūtile est puerīs ad loquendī facultātem, ideōque et retrō agere expositiōnem et ā mediā in utramque partem discurrere

    retelling what they have heard is good for children’s speech; so let them tell the story backwards, and run from the middle to either endQuint. 2.4.15

    In the entry for account

  • duplex inde fāma est: aliī proeliō victum Latīnum pācem cum Aenēā, deinde affīnitātem jūnxisse trādunt

    from here there are two versions: some say that Latinus, beaten in battle, made peace with Aeneas and then an alliance by marriageLiv. 1.1.6
